key_insight: For OCT choroid segmentation, learned image representations—especially retinal foundation models—are better quality gates than scalar NR-IQA metrics for predicting whether a scan will segment reliably.
clinical_relevance: A task-specific quality gate could help filter low-confidence retinal OCT scans before automated analysis, reducing segmentation failures in real-world workflows.
method: Evaluated 6,076 OCT B-scans from 80 subjects for task-specific quality gating.
Compared scalar NR-IQA metrics with supervised linear probes and unsupervised K-Means on pretrained embeddings.
Benchmarked general-purpose ImageNet models and retinal foundation models, including RETFound.
evidence_signal: Scalar metrics were weak (|r| < 0.20), ImageNet embeddings reached ROC-AUC up to 0.77, and RETFound reached about 0.81; retinal FMs also formed quality-aligned clusters beyond a patient-level permutation null.
watch_item: Performance was tested on choroid segmentation in a specific dataset, so thresholding or transfer to other OCT devices, tasks, or populations may require re-validation.
paper_title: Task-Specific Quality Gating for Retinal Optical Coherence Tomography B-Scans: Learned Representations Over Scalar Metrics in Choroid Segmentation
